title: Break a stale claim gate so unclaim and reopen free the claim
action: Per D2 (issue 108). `unclaim_cell`, `run_reopen` and `run_drop` in verbs/cells/handlers_close.rs already pass clear_claim_after=true to `mutate_cell`, which calls `release_claim_file_best_effort(root, id)` (verbs/cells/claims.rs). That helper returns silently when `acquire_gate` returns false (`return Ok(()); // GATE_HELD — best-effort caller never retries`). The gate is the create-new file `.bee/claims/<id>.adopting` holding `{"pid":…,"at":…}`; when a claiming process dies between acquire_gate and release_gate the file stays for ever (this repo has stale det-1/det-2/det-3/rel530-1/rel540-1/rel550-1 .adopting files, det-2's dated at the exact #108 claim time), so every later release skips and the claim row outlives the unclaim. Fix in claims.rs: when `acquire_gate` meets an existing gate file, treat it as stale and remove it (then try once more) when its `at` is older than 30 seconds, or its pid is not alive (on unix check /proc/<pid> or libc-free `std::path::Path::new("/proc").join(pid)` existence; on other targets use age only), or the file does not parse. Make `release_claim_file_best_effort` use `acquire_gate_with_retry` so a briefly-held live gate is waited out. Never break a fresh gate held by a live pid. Red first in verbs/cells/tests.rs: claim a cell (use the existing claim fixture — rg -n "fn .*claim" verbs/cells/tests.rs), write a stale `<id>.adopting` (pid 999999999, at one hour ago), run unclaim, and assert the claim file under .bee/claims is gone and a second claim succeeds; watch it fail before the fix. Add a test that a fresh gate with the current pid is not broken. No code comments. If cargo fails to compile in a file outside your files list, a sibling cell is mid-edit: wait 60 seconds and re-run; never edit that file.
